newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SUMMARY-Main Points of 1997/98 Australian budget.
newsitem.headline: SUMMARY-Main Points of 1997/98 Australian budget.

text.p: Following are the main features of the Australian government's 1997/98 (July/June) budget announced by Treasurer Peter Costello on Tuesday:
BUDGET DEFICIT, OUTLAYS AND REVENUE

*Underlying budget deficit (ie excluding asset sales) A$3.9 billion, 0.7 percent of gross domestic product, an improvement of A$3.0 billion on 1996/97. In 1998.3 percent of GDP) in underlying terms with increasing surpluses in outyears.
*New fiscal measures save A$352 million in 1997/98 and A$1.9 billion in 1998/99.

*Underlying outlays estimated at A$136.5 billion in 1996/97, A$137.2 billion in 1997/98 and A$140.8 billion in 1998/99. Revenue estimated A$129.6 billion in 1996/97, A$133.4 billion in 1997/98 and A$142.4 billion in 1998/99
KEY ECONOMIC FORECASTS

*GDP-A, the average measure of economic growth, to average 3.75 percent in 1997/98 compared with a forecast 3.25 percent in 1996/97 and 4.1 percent in 1995/96. But gross farm product to fall two percent vs nine percent growth in 1996/97.

*Consumer Price Index (CPI) to show one percent rise vs 1.25 percent in 1996/97 and 4.2 percent in 1995/96. Underlying inflation forecast at 2.0 percent, unchanged vs 1996/97, down from 3.2 percent in 1995/96.
*Employment to grow two percent after 1.25 percent growth in 1996/97 and 2.6 percent growth in 1995/96. Unemployment rate forecast at 8.0 percent by June quarter 1998 vs 8.75 percent in Q2 1997.
*Current account deficit projected at A$21 billion vs A$20 billion in 1996/97 and A$20.1 billion in 1995/96.
MEASURES

*No new taxes or increases in existing taxes. Costello says budget is designed to lift national savings and strengthen economic growth with medium term objective of achieving underlying budget balance.
*Tax rebate of 15 percent on savings, in two stages -- 7.5 percent from July 1, 1998 and full rebate (maximum A$450 per year) from July 1, 1999.
*No net borrowing requirement, government to repay over A$5 billion of debt in 1997/98.
*Bonus of up to A$31,540 offered to keep potential pensioners working for another five years from age 65 to 70.

*Budget papers show asset sales expected to total A$9.83 billion in 1997/98, implying the proceeds from the sale of one-third of telecoms carrier Telstra Corp (expected to raise more than A$8 billion) would be spread over two years.
OTHER

*Establishment of special A$1 billion fund to celebrate the centenary of the country's federation in 1901, including a long planned national museum in Canberra, to be spent in the five years from 1998/99.
*A$1.25 billion set aside to fund National Heritage Trust over six years.
*Crack-down on trading of franking credits and dividend streaming.

*Tightened spending on pharmaceutical benefits scheme, through the introduction of a base price scheme for similar drugs, resulting in expected savings of about A$696 million over the next four years.
*Government plans to amend withholding tax arrangements in an effort to reduce compliance costs for small businesses, resulting in additional revenue of A$330 million in 1998/99.
*Defence spending to increase to A$10.4 billion from A$10.0 billion, a two percent real rise.
COSTELLO COMMENTS

*Costello says during budget lockup that budget is a "very good effort by world standards," that the Reserve Bank would be "pretty impressed" by its fiscal restraint and the ratings agencies would like the planned reduction in debt. He made no comment on interest rates.
-- Canberra Bureau 61-6 273-2730
